
To understand fish growth and movement, and hence help with fish restoration, fish are sometimes marked with a fluorescent marker.

Different markers can be used, and one research study [@data:Carty2013:Trout] examined the use of TM200 treatment for rainbow trout, to determine its effect on fluorescence marks on the vertebrae of the fish.

In the description of the experimental design, the authors' study design required them to:


> ... allocate $180$ fish from the reference population to nine tanks ($6$ treated tanks and $3$ control tanks; $20$ fish/tank) and to assign a treatment condition (TM200 treated versus nontreated control) to each tank...
>
> --- @data:Carty2013:Trout, p. 35

1. Identify the *units of analysis* in this experiment.
2. Identify, with justification, the *type* of experiment.
